## Summary

The bug was a single off-by-one in `app/Http/Controllers/PostController.ts:16`: `index()` called `.paginate({ page: page + 1, perPage: 10 })`, but `page` (from `ListPostsQuerySchema`) is already 1-based and defaults to 1. That made the default `/posts` load page 2 of the ORM's pagination, and `?page=1` also load page 2, so the newest 10 posts were permanently skipped and no page ever reached them. Fixed by paginating with `page` directly instead of `page + 1`.

Added a new `posts.index` test suite in `tests/PostController.test.ts` that seeds 25 real posts via the `Post` model against the app's real (migrated + seeded) test SQLite database, then verifies via the Inertia JSON response that the default page and `?page=1` both return the 10 newest posts (highest ids) with `meta.currentPage === 1`, `from`/`to` of 1–10, and `links.prev === null`, and that `?page=2` returns the next 10 posts with `from`/`to` of 11–20. `bun run typecheck` and `bun test` both pass (5/5).
